\section{2026-10-07, 19:00: the v21 round complete on twelve seeds\secstatus{todo}}
\label{sec:round-complete}

\pfstep{The round ran to completion} Every one of the 104 relaunched runs reached epoch
1{,}199, at 42 to 45 s per epoch (56 s for the mask arm, whose schedule adds a masked pass),
and the 26 jobs ended themselves between 10:01 and 14:35 on 2026-10-07, inside the limit.
With pack 0's two survivors that is 106 finished runs over nine arms; the two missing
\texttt{S\_ref} splits (1 and 2) are the pack-0 runs stopped by hand after collapsing at
epochs 1{,}102 and 939 and never relaunched. \cref{tab:v21-round} is the readout:
per arm, the registered window (mean validation Pearson per feature over epochs 1{,}000 to
1{,}199) over every finished run and over the runs that did not collapse, and the paired
difference against \texttt{S\_ref} over the splits where neither run collapsed. Twelve
splits resolve a paired gap of about 0.02; the healthy pairs are fewer, so their resolution
is coarser still.

\input{tables/v21_round.tex}

\pfstep{Collapse decided the round more than any arm did} On the finished runs the collapse
counts are: Hadamard 10 of 12, null sink 6, no dropout 5, composite stack 4, rank-64 basis
3, reference 3 of 12 (one of the eight relaunched), and the mask schedule, the two-hop
propagation and the proteome head 0 of 12 each. The census over both rounds
(\cref{tab:collapse-census}, regenerated) now holds 64 dead stretches of 50 epochs or more,
of which 18 later returned to a spread of 0.05 (10 of the 22 between 50 and 99 epochs, 8 of
the 42 at 100 or more); the gradient norm at onset is a median 1.15 times the preceding
50-epoch mean over the 64, unchanged from the morning's reading. In the table the original
cohort's counts are low only because the swap killed those runs at epochs 270 to 930, before
most onsets.

\pfstep{What the arms say} Three results stand on all twelve seeds, the rest are inside the
noise.
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{The mask schedule is the one change that both removes collapse and raises
  the mean.} \texttt{S\_mask} (schedule 0, 10, 100, 1{,}000) collapsed on 0 of 12 and scores
  $0.094 \pm 0.028$ over all twelve seeds against $0.063 \pm 0.037$ for the reference over
  its ten; paired, $+0.033$ over the ten shared splits (8 above zero) and $+0.027$ over the
  nine healthy pairs (7 above). It launches late, at epochs 123 to 284 against 39 to 125 for
  every other arm, which is the schedule withholding labels early. It is the best arm on 5
  of the 12 splits; the reference is best on none.
  \item \textbf{The Hadamard operator is out.} \texttt{S\_hadam} collapsed on 10 of 12 and
  its two survivors sit at $0.017$ and $0.018$, $-0.040$ against the reference on both
  healthy pairs and $-0.055$ over all ten shared splits (1 above zero). With the v22
  warmup-arm reading ($-0.031$ on 3 of 3) that is two rounds and two machines against it.
  \item \textbf{The composite stack is the best model when it survives, and it survives
  two thirds of the time.} \texttt{S\_stack} (FUDT, CaLM and ProtT5 together) scores
  $0.096 \pm 0.019$ over its eight healthy runs, $+0.043$ on 6 of 6 healthy pairs, with the
  highest eval-mode train Pearson of the round (median 0.65 against 0.52) and the widest
  prediction spread (0.44 against 0.35). It collapsed on 4 of 12, so over all twelve seeds it
  is $0.071 \pm 0.046$, level with the reference. Hypothesis (untested): the stack and the
  mask schedule compose, since one adds capacity and the other removes the collapse.
  \item The null sink ($+0.017$ on 5 of 5 healthy pairs, 6 of 12 collapsed), the rank-64
  basis ($+0.008$, 5 of 7), the no-dropout arm ($+0.002$, 2 of 5, 5 collapsed) and the
  two-hop propagation ($+0.010$, 5 of 9) are within the twelve-seed resolution of the
  reference: not resolved, not null. Propagation collapsed on none but put 5 of 12 runs into
  a second low state that the collapse rule does not catch: spread 0.15 to 0.21, train
  Pearson 0.33 to 0.34, window $-0.004$ to $0.054$, against 0.31 to 0.46 spread and 0.56 to
  0.64 train Pearson on its other seven.
  \item \textbf{The proteome head sits at its sequence baseline.} \texttt{S\_prot} scores
  $0.066 \pm 0.021$ over twelve seeds, 0 collapsed, against the twelve-seed neighbor-average
  bar of $0.065$ on the same store (\cref{tab:baselines-both-label}); 6 of 12 runs are above
  it.
\end{itemize}

\pfstep{No arm mean clears the expression baseline} The twelve-seed neighbor average on
ProtT5 scores $0.110 \pm 0.017$ on this store. Every arm mean is below it, the best
(\texttt{S\_mask}, \texttt{S\_stack} healthy) by 0.015; 12 of the 94 finished expression
runs are above it, the best at $0.146$ (\texttt{S\_nodrop} and \texttt{S\_basis64} on
split 6). The model's per-split scores vary by $0.03$ to $0.05$ across seeds within an arm,
which is the same order as every contrast in the round except the Hadamard one.

\pfstep{Batch 128 on eleven seeds} IGB array 2426902 finished the batch-128 arm at the
unscaled rate on split seeds 4 to 11 (three runs per A40, 15.4 s per epoch; 10.4 s with two
on the card), which with the three GilaHyper seeds gives \texttt{F\_b128lr1} on eleven
seeds: window $0.051$ to $0.141$, mean $0.082$ (\cref{tab:night-arms}, regenerated), 0 of 11
collapsed. Paired against the batch-32 reference
on the same split seeds (the GilaHyper \texttt{F\_ref} on 0 to 2, the Delta \texttt{S\_ref}
on 4 to 11) it is $+0.013$ on 3 of 3 and $+0.020$ over 9 (6 above zero), $+0.014$ over the 8
pairs where the reference did not collapse (5 above): batch 128 at 3e-4 is level with or
slightly above batch 32 at a quarter of the epoch time, and the eleven seeds do not resolve
the sign. The batch-128 arm has now run 11 of 11 without collapse against the reference's
3 of 12 at batch 32 (hypothesis, untested as a contrast: the larger batch lowers the
collapse rate).

\pfstep{v20 at eight partitions} Tasks 4 and 5 of the conditioned round finished at
epoch 1{,}199 on \file{cabbi}; tasks 6 and 7 are at epochs 299 and 249, and tasks 8 to 11
wait under the two-task throttle. \cref{tab:v20-partial} is regenerated on the eight.
The proteome head conditioned on the strain's own expression is above the unconditioned
arm at the same epochs on 8 of 8 (the six complete partitions by $+0.022$ to $+0.079$,
mean $+0.050$; the two partial ones by $+0.008$ and $+0.054$) and above its
permuted-expression control on 8 of 8. The expression head conditioned on the proteome is
above the unconditioned arm on 7 of 8 (split 2 at $-0.004$; the complete six mean
$+0.024$) and above its permuted control on 8 of 8. The reading of the morning stands:
the gain is from the strain's own measurement, and both conditioned heads remain below
the per-partition ridge from the measured other modality.
